basis.statement: Air mode runs the Hall and the ICP on the delivered atmospheric gas; the primary ICP gas mode is G-REUSE (Hall exhaust / residual), with G-ATM / G-XE as declared contingency ICP-feed variants. Xe is a separate contingency supply mode, so air operation consumes no Xe. Hall-on-delivered-air is NOT_EVALUATED (credible Hall transport set EMPTY (members = []); P5-Xe not identifiable; P5-N2 v1 INCONCLUSIVE (permanent); no design-specific Hall map exists for any geometry). ICP AIR chemistry is INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE (12 tier-1 processes not verified; XE 4); the NO materiality bound is missing (A9.31 OQ-CHEM-02). The topology precedent is argon only; the authors' reactive-gas statement is a claim not shown in the paper (TK-30, TK-74). Hall sustainment on an O-bearing delivered feed cannot be supported by literature transfer (F-9; common to every Hall option).

basis.statement: No thermionic emitter: an RF / ICP electron source has 'no emitter to poison' (dossier, design rationale only). Exposed elements are the ICP dielectric tube, the shielded antenna, the ion-collecting electrode and the common Hall anode / channel. The topology precedent sputtered its stainless collector (sheath energies ~140-220 eV) and deposited metal films on the tube and Hall insulators (TK-70, TK-71). No accessed source measures dielectric, antenna or collector erosion under an air / AO plasma. AO life is a separate dedicated programme (owner row 132).

basis.statement: The cathode runs on Xe; no source shows a thermionic hollow cathode running on air, N2 or O2 (UNRESOLVED). Air operation therefore consumes Xe continuously, which makes Xe a nominal co-consumable. A5 accepted that (cathode Xe reserved, continuous discharge augmentation forbidden); A9.19 replaced it: Xe is the contingency / emergency supply mode, consistent with RFP-P17-05 ('an extra input system to take care any problems on board unforeseen problems'). Hall-on-air NOT_EVALUATED (common accelerator).

LaB6 emission degrades at O2 ~1e-5 Torr below 1440 C and tolerates up to 1e-4 Torr at 1570 C; BaO-W poisons at ~1e-7 Torr O2. The ambient AO directed flux at 180-230 km equals a 300 K gas at 2.1e-6 to 1.65e-5 Torr, the same order as the O2 degradation range; the attenuation by the cathode Xe flow, orifice and keeper has no source, and no atomic-O or N2 threshold exists for LaB6. Secondary reports of erosion / embrittlement after air or N2/O2 exposure (RI-LIFE-CATHODE-AIR-EXPOSURE). Mitigation by a 1843 K emitter floor (owner row 95) and a non-graphite keeper (row 94) at unquantified life / power cost.

evidence_status.evidence_class: measured thresholds on other cathodes + model-derived AO flux

basis.statement: Same H-1 class accelerator as ALT-B; thrust NOT_EVALUATED (credible Hall transport set EMPTY (members = []); P5-Xe not identifiable; P5-N2 v1 INCONCLUSIVE (permanent); no design-specific Hall map exists for any geometry). No neutralizer-imposed current cap is indicated for this current class (context: a 5 A nominal laboratory LaB6 cathode serves an SPT-100-class thruster).

Same slot set and numbers as bus_power_boundary_a9_v2 (a9_v1 is byte-identical except the configuration taxonomy) plus C1 heater / keeper / cathode-common slots INSTALLED in the retired hall_c1_reference column. Load-side analogs: heater 45-305 W at ignition (other LaB6 cathodes), keeper ~32-34 W (NEXT, inferred), laboratory heater left on 68-72 W (ECHT), low-power Hall cathodes up to 20 % of available power (secondary). P_bus NOT_EVALUATED.

A hollow cathode needs a continuous Xe flow. At the A5 design target 0.10 mg/s the cathode uses 5.4 kg Xe over 15,000 h (8.1 kg at the 0.15 mg/s test point); over the reference flows of other cathodes (P5 setpoint, SITAEL HC1 / HC3 ranges) 40 kg minus the cathode Xe spans -14 to 35.68 kg, so the indicator straddles the 40 kg limit (RI-MASS-CATHODE-XE, not verdict-bearing). In the mass/power v2 record the hall_c1_reference column's booked Xe terms exceed the 2 kg and 5 kg Xe cases (XE_CASE_BELOW_BOOKED_TERMS); only the 10 kg case has headroom. The C1 module itself has no allocation (partial 0.2 kg floor) and the dry columns are NOT comparable (mass v2). Conditional arithmetic (this lane): IF C1 flows at 0.10 mg/s, its Xe alone (5.4 kg) exceeds the 3.5 kg AL-05 + AL-06 allocation that ALT-B carries for the ICP and RF hardware, while ALT-B's 2 kg planning case is already 0.349 kg above 40 kg.

evidence_status.evidence_class: planning allocation + inferred arithmetic on other cathodes' flows

findings: No alternative has an admitted thrust, P_bus or closed mass; the comparison supplies no feasible region for any option, so it cannot by itself support category A or B.
No investigated alternative is better supported than ALT-B on any criterion with determining evidence; there is no determining evidence on any criterion for any option.

Where repository evidence supports a qualitative ordering, ALT-B is favoured on architecture / mechanism grounds for atmospheric-gas compatibility (no Xe consumable in air mode), AO / cathode exposure (no thermionic emitter), feed architecture (no continuous Xe branch) and, conditionally, Xe mass; ALT-A is favoured on evidence maturity for neutralization, controllability and neutralizer electrical power per ampere (Xe analogs).

ALT-C and ALT-D3 are excluded only on mechanism-level, probably robust grounds; ALT-D1 / ALT-D2 are historical and not physically eliminated; ALT-A is retired by owner decision, not by a physics veto.

The wet-mass DOES_NOT_CLOSE planning status of ALT-B is not relieved by switching to ALT-A: a continuous Xe cathode term at the 0.10 mg/s design target (5.4 kg) exceeds the 3.5 kg ICP / RF allocations it would replace, and ALT-A's booked Xe terms exceed the 2 and 5 kg cases (conditional, allocation-level).
